effects.log: You pay 100 taels. The painter refuses to change the faces. You let it go. Somehow you feel you won.

choices.text: Let the mural fade

effects.log: The faces fade. People still come. They say it is better when you cannot tell which is which.

events.text: The new Murim Ranking has been posted in every teahouse in the province. You are ranked forty-third. {npc} is ranked forty-second. The note beside {npc}'s name says: "Has never been beaten by the forty-third."

choices.text: Challenge {npc} to settle it

mem.note: took my place on the ranking

ok.log: You win before a crowd of two hundred. The next ranking moves you up. It also moves {npc} down to forty-fourth, and {npc} has not forgotten.

mem.note: kept my place on the ranking

fail.log: You lose before a crowd of two hundred. The note beside {npc}'s name is updated: "Twice."

choices.text: Go and find whoever writes the ranking

ok.log: The ranking is written by a retired clerk with a tea habit and strong opinions. You leave with tea and a better understanding of why nobody likes rankings.

fail.log: You do not find the clerk. You find {npc}, looking for the same clerk.

choices.text: Ignore it

effects.log: You train. {npc} cannot stand being ignored and visits three times to mention the ranking.

events.text: The new Murim Ranking. You are thirty-first. {npc} is thirtieth, again, by one place, and this time the note says: "The two have not met in four years. The ranking fears to separate them."

choices.text: Write to the ranking clerk asking to be ranked equal

mem.note: asked for us to share a place

effects.log: The next ranking has you both at thirty, side by side, with a note: "By request, and to avoid bloodshed."

choices.text: Fight {npc} again, for real

ok.log: You win. You are thirtieth. It feels exactly like being thirty-first.

fail.log: {npc} wins. You are thirty-first. {npc} sends you a cake.

choices.text: Have both your names struck off

effects.log: You and {npc} write a joint letter. The clerk is so moved that the ranking is reprinted with a blank line at thirty and thirty-one.

events.text: The ranking clerk has died, and in the clerk's papers, you are told, is a note on you and {npc}: "The best rivalry I ever ranked. I put one above the other each year only to see what they would do." The clerk's student asks what you would like done with it.

choices.text: Have it printed with the next ranking

effects.log: Teahouses read it aloud for a week. {npc} sends you a single word: "Typical."

choices.text: Ask for the note and keep it

effects.log: You keep it in the drawer with your letters from {npc}.

choices.text: Burn it, laughing

effects.log: Some things the world should not know. {npc} would agree, and would also want a copy.

events.text: An old general's tomb has been found in the hills, sealed with a lock that needs two bronze keys. One of the keys you bought years ago at a market stall, as a curiosity. The other, you learn, hangs on {npc}'s wall for the same reason, and {npc} has just learned about yours.

choices.text: Write to {npc} proposing to open it together

effects.log: {npc} replies by return: "Do not touch the door without me."

choices.text: Offer {npc} silver for the key

effects.log: {npc} returns your letter in pieces, with a promise to be at the tomb door first, and to bring a guard dog.

choices.text: Try to break the lock alone

mem.note: tried to open the tomb alone

ok.log: You break the outer bars, and a dart misses your ear. The inner door holds. {npc} hears about it.

mem.note: tried to open the tomb alone

fail.log: The lock fights back. You limp away from the door with a dart in your shoulder, and {npc} hears about it.

events.text: You stand before the old general's tomb with {npc}, each holding a key. The keys turn together. Inside are three rooms: the general's weapons, the general's silver, and a room with only a lamp and a scroll, the general's last manual. Behind you, you hear horses: a gang of tomb robbers has followed you up the mountain.

choices.text: Hold the door against the robbers together

mem.note: held the tomb door with me

ok.log: Back to back in the doorway, you send the robbers down the mountain. Afterwards you read the manual together by the general's lamp.

mem.note: held the tomb door with me

fail.log: You hold, barely. In the morning you have a manual each, half read, and wounds to compare.

choices.text: Take the manual and run, leaving {npc} with the robbers

mem.note: left me with the tomb robbers

effects.log: You run with the scroll. {npc} fights the robbers alone and lives. From that day you have an enemy, not a rival.

choices.text: Lock the tomb again with the robbers outside

effects.log: You turn the keys from inside. The robbers give up at dawn. You spend a strange quiet night in a dead general's house, reading.

events.text: The manual from the general's tomb has a last page you and {npc} never understood. This year {npc} writes: "I have it. The last page is not a technique. It is the general's apology to the soldiers buried in that hill. Come and read it with me."

choices.text: Go

mem.note: read the general's last page with me

effects.log: You read it together under the pines. It is long, and sad, and it changes the way you both hold a sword.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to send a copy

effects.log: The copy comes in {npc}'s hand. At the bottom {npc} has added: "Ours would be shorter. Do not make me write it."

choices.text: Take the keys back to the tomb and lock it for good

mem.note: locked the general's tomb for good

effects.log: You both turn the keys one last time and throw them in the river.

events.text: A ransom letter arrives addressed to you. The Black Bamboo bandits have taken {npc} on the mountain road and want 200 taels. The bandits explain, with poor spelling, that {npc} told them you were the only person who would pay.

choices.text: Pay the ransom

effects.log: You pay 200 taels. {npc} walks out of the bamboo with a black eye and says, very stiffly, "I told them you would not."

choices.text: Go into the bamboo and get {npc} out

mem.note: came into the Black Bamboo for me

ok.log: You find {npc} tied up and playing chess with the bandit chief. You win the fight. {npc} wins the chess game.

mem.note: came into the bamboo for me

fail.log: The bandits catch you too. You spend a week tied beside {npc} until the county guard arrives. It is the longest conversation you have ever had.

choices.text: Write back that you will not pay

effects.log: The bandits, disgusted, let {npc} go for nothing. {npc} arrives at your gate and says, "Not even ten taels?"

events.text: The bandit chief of the Black Bamboo has been captured and is to be tried. To everyone's surprise, {npc} has asked the court for mercy for the chief, and asks you to speak for the chief as well. "We played a great deal of chess," says {npc}.

choices.text: Speak for the bandit chief

mem.note: spoke for the bandit chief with me

effects.log: The chief is sent to work on the river dykes instead of the scaffold. {npc} visits every month with a chess board.

choices.text: Speak against the chief

effects.log: The chief is sent to the mines. {npc} does not speak to you for a season.

choices.text: Say nothing

effects.log: The court decides without you. {npc} wins the mercy alone, and is surprised you did not object.

events.text: The bandit chief of the Black Bamboo, released, has become a ferryman and a famous chess player. The chief invites you and {npc} to a game: "The two of you against me. My last tournament."

choices.text: Play as a pair with {npc}

mem.note: played chess as a pair with me

ok.log: You argue every move and win. The old chief laughs and gives you both a black bamboo board.

mem.note: played chess as a pair with me

fail.log: You lose. The old chief laughs and gives you both a black bamboo board anyway.

choices.text: Watch {npc} play the chief

effects.log: {npc} loses three games and wins the fourth. You have never seen {npc} so happy to win anything.

choices.text: Bring the county guard who caught the chief, as a joke

effects.log: The old guard and the old bandit end up playing all night. You and {npc} walk home, forgotten.

events.text: A Demonic Cult raiding party has cut the road at Red Pine Pass and taken the travellers' inn. The county has no soldiers to send. Two martial artists are in the nearest town: you, and {npc}, who arrived yesterday and has been pretending not to see you.
events.arc: Back to Back at Red Pine Pass

choices.text: Go to the pass with {npc}

mem.note: fought back to back with me at Red Pine

ok.log: Back to back, all night, among the burning pines. At dawn the raiders are gone and the travellers are free. Neither of you can stand. Neither of you will admit it.

mem.note: fought back to back with me at Red Pine

fail.log: You hold the inn door until the raiders tire. {npc} carries you out on one shoulder, bleeding, cursing your weight.

choices.text: Go alone, before {npc}

mem.note: went to Red Pine without me

ok.log: You break the raiders alone. {npc} arrives at noon to find it done and does not speak to you for a year.

mem.note: came to Red Pine after me

fail.log: You are losing when {npc} arrives. {npc} says nothing. {npc} simply takes your left side.

choices.text: Gather the townsfolk with bows first

mem.note: led the town to Red Pine

effects.log: It takes a day. You go up with forty farmers and {npc} in front. The raiders run from the sight of so many hoes.

events.text: A cult assassin has come for you, and you only know because {npc} intercepted the assassin on a rooftop at midnight and is now sitting in your courtyard with a cut on one arm and a dagger on the table. "Red Pine," {npc} says. "They remember. So do I."
events.arc: Back to Back at Red Pine Pass

choices.text: Bind the wound and pour the tea

effects.log: You bind the arm. {npc} drinks the tea. Neither of you says thank you. Both of you mean it.

choices.text: Go after whoever sent the assassin, with {npc}

mem.note: hunted the cult hall master with me

ok.log: The hall master who sent the killer is in a mountain shrine. After that night, the cult does not send anyone else to the county.

mem.note: hunted the cult hall master with me

fail.log: The hall master escapes. So do you, barely. The cult remembers that too.

choices.text: Insist on paying {npc} for the protection

mem.note: tried to pay me for Red Pine

effects.log: You leave 30 taels on the table. {npc} leaves it on the step when going. Neither of you mentions it.

events.text: The travellers' inn at Red Pine Pass has been rebuilt and a stone set at its door: "Here two who could not stand each other stood together." The innkeeper's grandchild has invited you both to the anniversary. It is twenty years.
events.arc: Back to Back at Red Pine Pass

choices.text: Go, and stand at the door together

mem.note: stood at the Red Pine stone with me

effects.log: The whole county comes. You stand by the stone. {npc} stands on your left, as before.

choices.text: Go, and find the burnt pine where you held the door

effects.log: The tree is still there, black on one side, green on the other. {npc} is already sitting under it.

choices.text: Send your regrets and a gift

effects.log: You send a lantern for the door. Later {npc} writes: "The lantern is the wrong colour. The inn loves it."

events.text: Across the province, {npc} has been telling everyone that you once saved {his} life in the Black Mountains. You have never been to the Black Mountains. Your fame grows by the week, and nobody believes your denials.

choices.text: Go and ask {npc} why

ok.log: {npc} looks at the floor. "Somebody did save me. I never learned who. It was easier to say it was you than to say I owed a stranger."

fail.log: {npc} shrugs. "It is a good story. Be grateful."

choices.text: Enjoy the fame

effects.log: Hosts serve you their best dishes and ask about the Black Mountains. You improvise. It is a good story.

choices.text: Deny it in public, loudly

effects.log: People think you are modest. Your fame grows anyway. {npc} is furious that you made the story worse.

events.text: A stranger arrives at your door: a quiet herbalist from the Black Mountains, who has heard the story going round and wants you to know, gently, that it was the herbalist who pulled {npc} out of the river that winter. The herbalist does not want anything. Only the truth.

choices.text: Take the herbalist to {npc}

mem.note: brought me the one who saved me

effects.log: {npc} looks at the herbalist for a long time and then bows to the ground. You leave them alone. You have never seen {npc} cry.

choices.text: Thank the herbalist and send them away quietly

effects.log: The story stays yours. The herbalist goes home. You feel it every time you are praised.

choices.text: Tell the story yourself, the true one, at the teahouse

effects.log: The true story is better. The herbalist becomes famous. {npc} sends the herbalist a cartload of medicine every year after.

events.text: {npc} has paid for a small hall of medicine in the Black Mountains, run by the herbalist. Over the door: "Built by one who lied about being saved, for the one who saved." {npc} asks you to come and open it, "since you were in the lie."

choices.text: Open the hall with {npc}

mem.note: opened the herbalist's hall with me

effects.log: The herbalist cuts the ribbon. You and {npc} carry the first chest of medicine in together.

choices.text: Send silver for the hall

effects.log: You send 30 taels. The hall buys a second stove with it, which the herbalist names after you.

choices.text: Decline: it is {npc}'s debt

mem.note: let me pay my own debt

effects.log: {npc} understands. You hear the hall is good. You go, years later, as a patient.

events.text: {npc} is getting married, and a red invitation has come to your house, written in {npc}'s own hand: "You will sit at the second table. You will not make a speech. You will not fight anyone."

choices.text: Go, and keep to all three conditions

mem.note: came to my wedding and behaved

effects.log: It is very difficult. You manage. {npc} is so astonished that {npc} comes to your table to check you are not ill.

choices.text: Go, and give a speech anyway

mem.note: made a speech at my wedding

ok.log: You tell the story of the kite war. The hall weeps with laughter. {npc} glares, then laughs, then raises a cup to you.

mem.note: made a speech at my wedding

fail.log: Your speech is too honest. The new in-laws stop smiling. {npc} does not.

choices.text: Send a gift and stay away

mem.note: sent a gift but did not come

effects.log: You send a carved pair of mandarin ducks worth 30 taels. {npc} keeps them by the bed and tells everyone they were from a cousin.

events.text: {npc}'s marriage is in trouble, and {npc}'s spouse, of all people, has come to see you: "You are the only one who has ever been able to make that stubborn fool listen. Please. Talk to {him}."

choices.text: Go and talk to {npc}

ok.log: You find {npc} on the roof. You talk for half the night. The marriage mends. {npc} tells everyone you said nothing useful.

fail.log: You say the wrong thing. {npc} throws you off the roof, gently. Later the marriage mends anyway, and nobody tells you how.

choices.text: Refuse: it is not your place

effects.log: The spouse goes home. {npc}, you hear, is grateful you stayed out, and furious you were asked.

choices.text: Talk to the spouse instead

effects.log: You tell the spouse about {npc}, the real {npc}, the one who climbs trees and holds grudges. The spouse goes home understanding a great deal more.

events.text: {npc}'s spouse has died. {npc} has asked that you, and nobody else, read the farewell at the funeral, "because you are the only one who ever argued with both of us."

choices.text: Read the farewell

mem.note: read the farewell for my spouse

effects.log: Your voice shakes once. {npc} stands beside you the whole time. Afterwards {npc} says only, "Second table. No speech. You broke both."

choices.text: Ask {npc} to read it, and stand beside {him}

mem.note: stood beside me at the funeral

effects.log: {npc} reads it. When the voice breaks, you put a hand on {npc}'s shoulder, and the voice goes on.

choices.text: Send your farewell in writing

effects.log: The letter is read out by a nephew. It is good. It is not you standing there.

events.text: {npc} has fallen ill and sends for you urgently, believing the end has come. From the bed, {npc} confesses a secret held since childhood: it was {npc} who stole your first wooden sword and threw it down the well. "Forgive me," {npc} whispers. "I have hated myself for forty years."

choices.text: Forgive {npc}

effects.log: {npc} weeps, and sleeps, and in the morning the fever has broken. {npc} is going to live. This is going to be very awkward.

choices.text: Confess your own secret in return

effects.log: You confess that you were the one who put the frog in {npc}'s tea at the festival when you were nine. {npc} laughs so hard the fever breaks.

choices.text: Say you knew all along

effects.log: You did not know. You say it anyway. {npc} glares and, out of sheer annoyance, recovers.

events.text: {npc} has made a complete recovery, and is mortified. Since the deathbed, {npc} has avoided you in the street, ducked behind carts and once hidden in a fishmonger's barrel. The whole town has noticed.

choices.text: Corner {npc} and tell the well story to everyone in the teahouse

mem.note: told the well story in public

effects.log: The teahouse roars. {npc} goes red, then laughs, then buys a round. The barrel is never mentioned.

choices.text: Leave a new wooden sword on {npc}'s step

mem.note: left a wooden sword on my step

effects.log: The next morning there are two wooden swords on yours, one new and one very old and rotten, pulled up out of the well.

choices.text: Pretend it never happened

effects.log: {npc} does too. It works. You both act as if nothing happened for the rest of your lives, which is its own kind of intimacy.

events.text: This time you are the one who is ill, and the physician's face is grave. You send for {npc}. {npc} arrives at a run and sits by the bed with a face like stone.

choices.text: Confess something real

effects.log: You tell {npc} the truest thing you know: that you were glad, all your life, to have someone to measure yourself by. {npc} holds your wrist. You do not die. You are both embarrassed for a year.

choices.text: Tell {npc} you are not going to forgive the well

effects.log: {npc} laughs so loud the physician comes in. Your fever breaks that night. {npc} takes the credit.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to look after something for you

effects.log: You give {npc} the old rotten wooden sword. You recover. {npc} refuses to give it back.

events.text: {npc} has given up the sword for the brush and been appointed inspector of the county. The first thing the new inspector does is to send you a summons: your accounts, your land deeds and your tax receipts, by the end of the month.

choices.text: Bring everything, in perfect order

ok.log: Your books are spotless. {npc} reads every page and is clearly disappointed.

fail.log: There is a mistake in the third year. {npc} fines you 30 taels with a face of perfect neutrality.

choices.text: Bring everything, and a cake

effects.log: {npc} eats the cake during the inspection. Your books are fine. {npc} still finds a smudge.

choices.text: Refuse: {npc} is doing this out of spite

effects.log: {npc} is not doing it out of spite. Or not only. The fine is heavier than the books would have been.

events.text: The county's magistrate, {npc}'s superior, is stealing from the flood funds, and {npc} has found out. {npc} comes to you at night: there is no one else in the county who will not be bought or frightened. "You are the only person I know who has never once done what I wanted."

choices.text: Help {npc} take the evidence to the capital

mem.note: rode to the capital with me

ok.log: The hired men catch you on the road. You deal with them. The evidence reaches the capital. The magistrate is removed.

mem.note: rode to the capital with me

fail.log: You lose the first set of ledgers on the road, but {npc} sewed a second set into a saddle. It is enough.

choices.text: Hide the evidence in your house

effects.log: The magistrate's men search {npc}'s house and find nothing. Your house is too obvious for anybody to think of.

choices.text: Advise {npc} to leave it

mem.note: told me to leave the flood money

effects.log: {npc} looks at you a long moment. "That is the first thing you have ever told me to do that I will not do." {npc} goes alone.

events.text: {npc} has risen to the provincial court, and writes: the province needs an honest examiner for the martial academies, someone who cannot be bought. {npc} has put forward your name, "out of spite."

choices.text: Accept the post

effects.log: You are a terrible, honest examiner. Bribes are returned with lectures. {npc} receives complaints about you daily and files them with great pleasure.

choices.text: Decline, and name someone better

effects.log: {npc} appoints your choice and sends you a single line: "Coward. Good choice."

choices.text: Accept, on condition that {npc} is examined first

effects.log: {npc} accepts. You examine {npc} for two days. {npc} passes. Barely.

events.text: The Lantern Festival contest on the river: whoever floats the most beautiful lantern wins a year of free tea at the Willow House. {npc} has hired a famous paper-cutter. You have a pot of glue and a dream.

choices.text: Make a lantern yourself, all night

ok.log: Your lantern is a lopsided carp with real scales of cut paper. The crowd loves it. {npc}'s perfect phoenix comes second, which is somehow worse than losing.

fail.log: Your carp sinks with great dignity. The crowd applauds it all the way down.

choices.text: Hire a better paper-cutter

effects.log: You pay 20 taels. Now two famous paper-cutters are feuding and the lanterns are glorious and nobody remembers who paid for which.

choices.text: Float a plain lantern with a wish on it

effects.log: You do not win. You wish for something you do not tell anybody. A year later it comes true.

events.text: The Willow House teahouse, which gives the lantern prize, has a new problem: you and {npc}, between you, have taken the prize so many times that nobody else enters. The owner begs you both to judge this year instead.

choices.text: Judge fairly

mem.note: judged the lanterns fairly with me

effects.log: You argue for an hour and give the prize to a child's lantern shaped like a cabbage. It is the right answer. {npc} agrees, which is alarming.

choices.text: Enter in secret under another name

ok.log: You win under the name Old Turnip. {npc}, judging, recognises your glue and says nothing.

fail.log: {npc} recognises your glue and disqualifies you in front of everyone.

choices.text: Refuse: you are not done winning

effects.log: You enter. {npc} enters. Nobody else does. You both win, the owner decides, and pays twice.

events.text: A small boat of lanterns floats down the river at the festival: a cabbage, a carp, a phoenix, and a dozen others, one for every year of the contest. A note pinned to the pier in {npc}'s hand reads: "We were very silly. It was very good."

choices.text: Float one more lantern beside them

effects.log: You make a carp again. It still leans. You watch it follow the others down the river until it is a spark.

choices.text: Find {npc} on the pier

effects.log: {npc} is sitting on the end of the pier with a pot of tea and two cups. You drink in silence and watch the lanterns.

choices.text: Write a note of your own under {npc}'s

effects.log: You write: "You were very silly." Under that, the next morning, someone has written: "Both of us."

events.text: {npc} turns up at your gate, very politely, to borrow your horse, Chestnut, "for a short journey of the utmost importance." You have never heard {npc} say please before.

choices.text: Lend Chestnut

effects.log: {npc} rides away with a strange expression. Two months later, Chestnut comes back fat, glossy and in foal.

choices.text: Ask what the journey is

ok.log: {npc} is going to fetch a physician for an old aunt in the hills. You give Chestnut and a bag of feed. Chestnut comes back fat, glossy and in foal.

fail.log: {npc} will not say, and walks to the hills instead.

choices.text: Refuse

effects.log: {npc} walks. It takes four extra days. You hear later the journey was to fetch a physician, and the old aunt lived anyway, no thanks to you.

events.text: Chestnut's foal has been born: a leggy, wild-eyed colt with a white blaze. {npc} arrives the same day with a document claiming the father was {npc}'s stallion and the colt, therefore, half {npc}'s.

choices.text: Agree to share the colt

effects.log: The colt lives a month at each house and grows up confused and spoiled. Both of you are hopelessly attached to it.

choices.text: Take it to the magistrate

mem.note: won the colt at the magistrate

ok.log: The magistrate rules the foal goes with the mare. {npc} visits the colt every week, sulking.

fail.log: The magistrate rules half the colt is {npc}'s. Which half is not specified. It takes a year to decide.

choices.text: Give {npc} the colt, as the price of the stallion

effects.log: {npc} is speechless. The colt grows into the fastest horse in the county and is named, to your enormous annoyance, after you.

events.text: The colt is a famous old warhorse now, grey at the muzzle, and too slow to race. {npc} writes to ask where the horse should spend its last years: "At yours or mine. It has never decided. Neither have we."

choices.text: Bring the old horse to your stable

effects.log: The horse spends its last years in your pasture, and {npc} visits so often that your servants start setting a third place.

choices.text: Let it stay with {npc}

effects.log: You visit every spring with a bag of apples. The old horse remembers you before {npc} does.

choices.text: Ride it once more together, to the hills

mem.note: rode to the hills with me

effects.log: The old horse carries you both, slowly, to the old aunt's village. Nobody there remembers the journey. The horse does.

events.text: A wanted poster has gone up across three counties: a highway robber, 100 taels reward. The name on it is {npc}'s. The face on it is yours. Neither of you is a highway robber, and the bounty hunters cannot read.

choices.text: Go with {npc} to the magistrate to clear it up

ok.log: The magistrate, the painter and a bounty hunter argue for a day. A new poster goes up, with the right face of the wrong person.

fail.log: The magistrate is away. Three bounty hunters are not. You and {npc} spend a week hiding in a barn.

choices.text: Catch the real robber

ok.log: You catch the real robber, who looks like neither of you, and collect your own bounty.

fail.log: The real robber gets away, laughing, with your purse.

choices.text: Grow a beard, or the nearest thing

effects.log: Nobody recognises you. Nobody wants to. {npc}, meanwhile, is arrested twice in a week.

events.text: The bounty hunters have found a cleverer solution: they have arrested you both, on the grounds that one of you must be guilty. You are now in the same cell, with the real robber in the next one, who is enjoying it enormously.

choices.text: Break out together

ok.log: You work the bars loose in two nights. The real robber begs to come. You leave the robber for the magistrate, tied in a bow.

fail.log: You break a finger on the bars. {npc} laughs until the jailer comes.

choices.text: Wait for the magistrate's return

mem.note: waited in the cell with me

effects.log: The magistrate is back in a week. In that week you and {npc} play a hundred games of finger-guessing and talk about everything.

choices.text: Bribe the jailer

effects.log: You pay 30 taels. The jailer lets you out. {npc}, too proud to be bribed out, stays the week.

events.text: The old poster has become a collector's piece, a famous mistake. A merchant in the capital has offered to buy it, and needs both of you to sign it. The offer is 200 taels. {npc} has already signed with a joke under it.

choices.text: Sign, and split the money

effects.log: You sign under {npc}'s joke with a worse joke. The merchant frames it. It hangs in a teahouse in the capital to this day.

choices.text: Sign, and give your half to the jailer's widow

effects.log: The jailer died last spring. The widow sends a jar of plums every year after.

choices.text: Refuse to sign: you are not a curiosity

effects.log: The merchant buys it unsigned for less. {npc} forges your name, perfectly, which is the most worrying part.

events.text: {npc} has been exiled to the northern frontier for striking a prince's cousin in a dispute that, you hear, was about a dog. The cart leaves at dawn. You are the only person at the town gate.

choices.text: Give {npc} your winter coat

mem.note: gave me a coat at the gate

effects.log: You take it off and throw it into the cart. {npc} catches it, looks at you, and says nothing all the way out of sight.

choices.text: Promise to petition for a pardon

effects.log: "Do not bother," says {npc}. Then, from the cart, very quietly: "Bother."

choices.text: Ask about the dog

effects.log: The dog was being kicked. {npc} kicked back. The prince's cousin went into a pond. You laugh. {npc} laughs. The guards are disgusted with you both.

events.text: A letter from the frontier, the first in three years, in {npc}'s hand: the fort is cold, the commander is a fool, the bandits across the border are better organised than the army, and {npc} is now the only person in the fort who is listened to. At the end: "Send tea. Real tea. Not the stuff you drink."

choices.text: Send the best tea you can find

effects.log: You send 20 taels of the best leaf. The next letter says the tea was the second worst {npc} has ever had, and asks for more.

choices.text: Petition the court for a pardon

ok.log: The prince's cousin, it turns out, has since been in two more ponds. The court is persuadable. A pardon is signed.

fail.log: The petition goes nowhere. You keep writing. So does {npc}.

choices.text: Go north and see {npc}

ok.log: The road takes a month. {npc} sees you through the fort gate and drops a bucket.

fail.log: The road nearly kills you. {npc} nurses you back to health in the fort, scolding the whole time.

events.text: The frontier war is over, and the hero of the northern fort is coming home: {npc}, pardoned, honoured, older. The town has hung banners. {npc}'s first letter from the road says only: "Will you be at the gate?"

choices.text: Be at the gate

effects.log: You are the first person {npc} sees. You are still the only one at the gate who {npc} looks for.

choices.text: Be at the gate, with the dog

effects.log: You have kept the kicked dog all these years, old now and grey. The dog remembers {npc}. Everybody at the gate weeps, including the guards.

choices.text: Stay away, so the town can have {npc}

effects.log: {npc} comes to your house that night, alone, and sits on your step until you open the door.

events.text: {npc} has taken a bad fall from a horse and woken with no memory of the last thirty years. The physician says it may return or may not. In the meantime, {npc} has asked to see "my dearest friend," and given your name.

choices.text: Go, and be {npc}'s dearest friend

mem.note: came when I had forgotten everything

effects.log: {npc} hugs you. You have no idea what to do with your arms. The physician watches with great interest.

choices.text: Go, and tell {npc} the truth about the two of you

effects.log: {npc} listens, astonished. "Rivals? For thirty years? That sounds exhausting. Were we any good?"

choices.text: Do not go

mem.note: did not come when I asked

effects.log: {npc} asks for you every day. The physician sends you a note every day, more and more disapproving.

events.text: {npc}, still without memory, wants to learn the martial arts again "from the person who knows me best." Every morning {npc} turns up at your gate in old practice clothes, beaming, and calls you "dear friend".

choices.text: Teach {npc} honestly

effects.log: You teach {npc} everything, including the moves you used to hide. {npc} learns fast. You find you are enjoying yourself.

choices.text: Teach {npc} your own style, so you will always win

effects.log: You teach {npc} to fight like you. It is very strange to be beaten by your own moves.

choices.text: Tell {npc} to go to another teacher

effects.log: {npc} goes to another teacher, sadly. Within a month {npc} has picked a fight with the other teacher, and nobody is surprised.

events.text: One morning {npc} arrives at your gate, stops dead, and stares at you. The memory has come back. All of it. Including the last three years.

choices.text: Ask whether {npc} would like to go on as friends

effects.log: {npc} is silent a long time. "You were a terrible friend," {npc} says, "and an even better rival. We can try." It works, mostly.

choices.text: Challenge {npc} at once

mem.note: fought me the day I remembered

ok.log: You fight like the old days. {npc} wins with one of your own moves. "Thank you for teaching me that," {npc} says, very coldly, and then laughs.

mem.note: fought me the day I remembered

fail.log: You win, but {npc} uses one of your own moves twice. "Thank you for teaching me that," {npc} says, very coldly, and then laughs.

choices.text: Say nothing and pour the tea, as you have every morning

mem.note: poured the tea as if nothing had changed

effects.log: {npc} sits. Drinks. Neither of you mentions it, ever. The mornings go on.

events.text: {npc} has written a memoir, The Road of the Sword, and it is selling in every bookshop in the province. You appear on two hundred pages. On most of them you lose. On page ninety you are described as having "the footwork of a startled goose."

choices.text: Write a reply, chapter by chapter

ok.log: Your reply, The Road of the Sword, Corrected, sells nearly as well. The goose is answered by a donkey. Readers buy both.

fail.log: Your reply is accurate and dull. Nobody buys it. {npc} buys three copies to give away as a joke.

choices.text: Go and confront {npc} at a reading

ok.log: You heckle from the back. The audience thinks it is part of the show. You both get invited to the next reading in the capital.

fail.log: You heckle. {npc} reads page ninety aloud, with gestures.

choices.text: Read it all, quietly, and say nothing

effects.log: It is a good book, a little unfair, a little sad. On the last page {npc} writes that every road needs someone walking the other way.

events.text: The memoir sold so well that the printer wants a second book. {npc} has a condition: it must be written together, one chapter each, to settle every quarrel once and for all. The printer has already announced it.

choices.text: Write it together

mem.note: wrote the second book with me

effects.log: You quarrel over every chapter. The book has footnotes in which each of you disputes the other. It is the best book either of you has written.

choices.text: Agree, and then write every chapter so that you win

effects.log: The book is full of your victories. {npc} adds footnotes that say "No." Readers adore the footnotes.

choices.text: Refuse: the first one was enough

mem.note: would not write the second book

effects.log: {npc} writes it alone. You are kinder in it than in the first. You notice.

events.text: A young storyteller has turned the two books into a play, and you and {npc} are invited to the first night in the capital. You will both sit in the front row, watching yourselves be played by people who are much better-looking.

choices.text: Go, and sit beside {npc}

effects.log: The actor playing you is wonderful as a startled goose. At the end both actors bow to the front row, and the whole theatre stands up for two old fools.

choices.text: Go backstage and correct the actors

effects.log: The actors are delighted. The second night's play is more accurate, and worse. {npc} takes you to task for it.

choices.text: Stay home and read the books again

effects.log: You read both, side by side. In the margin of page ninety, in your own copy, someone once wrote: "Not a goose. A crane." It is {npc}'s hand.

events.text: The province holds a tournament for masters past fifty, with padded spears, a physician on every corner and a great deal of complaining. You enter, to see who else has. On the list, of course, is {npc}.

choices.text: Win your way through

ok.log: Four bouts. Four victories. Five complaints, two about knees. {npc} wins on the other side, swearing at the stairs.

fail.log: You lose in the second round to a retired fishmonger. {npc} wins on the other side, and you are almost glad.

choices.text: Spend the tournament gossiping with the other old masters

effects.log: You learn more about the old days in three days than you knew in thirty years. Half the stories are about you. Half of those are wrong.

choices.text: Withdraw and watch {npc}

effects.log: {npc} fights with the same dropped shoulder from fifty years ago. Nobody else notices. You do.

events.text: The final of the Old Masters' Tournament is you against {npc}, because of course it is. The crowd is large, the physicians are nervous, and someone has brought a chair for each of you.

choices.text: Fight for real

mem.note: fought me for real in the old masters' final

ok.log: You win. {npc} lies on the boards, laughing at the sky, too stiff to rise. You lie down beside {npc} because you are too stiff as well.

mem.note: fought me for real in the old masters' final

fail.log: {npc} wins. You lie on the boards and laugh until the physician runs over.

choices.text: Sit in the chairs and argue instead

mem.note: sat out the final with me

effects.log: You argue about a fight in your twenties for an hour. The judges declare it the best final in the tournament's history.

choices.text: Concede before the first blow

effects.log: {npc} wins, and refuses the prize until you share it. It is a cake. You share it.

events.text: The Old Masters' Tournament has a new rule, the Rule of the Two Chairs: in the final, each fighter may sit down once. The tournament asks if it may name the rule after you and {npc}.

choices.text: Agree

mem.note: let the rule be named after us

effects.log: Old masters sit in your chairs all over the province now. {npc} complains that the rule should have been named after {npc} alone.

choices.text: Agree, if the chairs are good ones

effects.log: The chairs are very good ones, of yellow elm. You and {npc} test them at length.

choices.text: Decline: the chairs were {npc}'s idea

effects.log: It was not {npc}'s idea. {npc} knows. The rule is named the Rule of {npc}'s Chairs. You enjoy it more than {npc} does.

events.text: It rains for a week, and a letter comes from {npc}: the old scar on {his} shoulder, the one you gave {him} in your twenties, aches in this weather, "as it has done every rainy day for thirty years. I thought you should know."

choices.text: Send a balm, with an apology

mem.note: sent a balm for the old wound

effects.log: You send a jar of tiger balm worth 10 taels. The reply: "It does not help. Send another."

choices.text: Write back about your own old wound

effects.log: {npc} gave you yours the same year. You compare scars by letter for a month, like old soldiers.

choices.text: Visit with a physician

effects.log: The physician you pay 20 taels for says the wound is only age, and also that you two should be ashamed of yourselves.

events.text: {npc} writes again, in a different mood. A young physician has offered to take the old scar away with a new needle method. "But then I would have nothing of yours," {npc} writes. "Tell me what to do."

choices.text: Tell {npc} to have it healed

mem.note: told me to heal the scar

effects.log: {npc} has it healed. Then, you hear, gets a small sword tattooed on the shoulder where the scar was.

choices.text: Tell {npc} to keep it

mem.note: told me to keep the scar

effects.log: {npc} keeps it. Every rainy day, for the rest of your lives, a letter comes. You always answer.

choices.text: Have your own healed, and let {npc} choose after

effects.log: Your scar is gone. Your shoulder is lighter. {npc} keeps the old one, out of what {npc} calls "loyalty to one of us."

events.text: A rainy day. No letter from {npc} today. Or tomorrow. On the third day a servant comes instead: {npc} is ill and has asked for "the one who knows about rain".

choices.text: Go at once

effects.log: {npc} is propped up on cushions. "It aches," {npc} says, and pulls aside the robe to show you the old scar, and laughs, and the fever goes down.

choices.text: Go, with the old balm

effects.log: You rub the balm into the old scar. It does nothing, as always. {npc} sleeps for the first time in three days.

choices.text: Send a letter about the rain

effects.log: You write the longest letter of your life. The servant reads it to {npc}, who says it is too long.

events.text: A young swordsman has been going round the province claiming to have defeated both you and {npc} in a single afternoon at Lotus Bridge. The braggart has never met either of you. Crowds follow wherever the tale is told. People are beginning to look at you strangely.
events.arc: The Upstart Who Beat You Both

choices.text: Find the braggart and issue a challenge

ok.log: The braggart does not recognise you until landing in the canal. The crowd that was following the braggart follows you instead.

fail.log: The braggart is better than the tale suggested, and now really has beaten one of you.

choices.text: Write to {npc} proposing you deal with this together

mem.note: dealt with the braggart with me

effects.log: {npc} replies by return: "Lotus Bridge. Noon. Bring your old footwork."

choices.text: Ignore it

effects.log: The tales grow. In the latest one, the braggart beat you both and then {npc}'s grandmother.

events.text: The young braggart has agreed to meet you and {npc} at Lotus Bridge, in front of half the province, to prove the tale. Nobody expected the two of you to come together. The braggart looks, for the first time, nervous.
events.arc: The Upstart Who Beat You Both

choices.text: Fight one after the other, as the tale claimed

ok.log: You go first. {npc} does not get a turn. "Typical," {npc} says, and tips the braggart gently into the river anyway.

fail.log: You lose. {npc} wins. The tale is now half true, and you hear about it for years.

choices.text: Offer to teach the braggart instead

mem.note: took on the braggart with me

effects.log: The braggart stares at two old masters offering lessons and bursts into tears: it was all for a meal and a name. Two teachers, one student, endless quarrels.

choices.text: Let {npc} deal with it

effects.log: {npc} ends it in three moves and then turns to the crowd: "My rival could have done it in two."

events.text: The braggart from Lotus Bridge has grown into a fine swordsman, and has written a true account of that day, saying the two old masters were less like enemies than like an old married couple.
events.arc: The Upstart Who Beat You Both

choices.text: Laugh

effects.log: You laugh until you cough. {npc} sends a letter: "Have it corrected. We were never that nice to each other."

choices.text: Demand a correction

effects.log: The correction says: "Less like a married couple than like two cats in a sack." {npc} approves.

choices.text: Send the swordsman a gift for telling the truth

effects.log: You send 20 taels. So, you learn later, did {npc}.

events.text: {npc} has decided, being old, to plan {his} own funeral, and has asked you to give the eulogy, "because you are the only one who will not lie." The rehearsal is next week. {npc} will attend.

choices.text: Write a true eulogy

effects.log: You write it all down: the kite, the vase, the bridge, the long game. It is very long. {npc} cries at the rehearsal, and then corrects six details.

choices.text: Write a flattering eulogy, as a joke

effects.log: {npc} listens to a page of lies about {his} wisdom and modesty and starts to laugh, and cannot stop, and you have to call a physician.

choices.text: Refuse: you intend to die first

effects.log: {npc} accepts this as a challenge. You both take up a tonic of ginseng and stubbornness.

events.text: {npc} has kept changing the funeral plans: the coffin, the music, the guests, the route. This is the fifth rehearsal. {npc} is lying in the coffin to test the cushion. "Speak," {npc} says. "I am listening."

choices.text: Give the eulogy into the coffin

effects.log: You speak. {npc} sits up halfway through to argue about the bridge. The undertaker leaves.

choices.text: Climb in and lie down too, to test the other side

mem.note: lay in the coffin with me

effects.log: Two old masters lying in a coffin, arguing about cushions. The undertaker's apprentice runs to fetch half the village.

choices.text: Tell {npc} to stop rehearsing and live

effects.log: {npc} climbs out, slowly, and goes for a walk in the hills, and comes back with a fish.

events.text: The funeral is not a rehearsal. {npc} has died in the night, peacefully, old, and has left instructions, a purse for the musicians, and a note for you: "No changes. Speak."

choices.text: Speak

effects.log: You speak, without the paper, for a long time. You say everything. At the end you find you have kept to every detail {npc} corrected. Then you go home and sit very still.

choices.text: Speak, and change one thing

effects.log: You change the end of the bridge story, so that {npc} is the one who saves you. Nobody alive knows the difference. You are fairly sure {npc} would have allowed it.

choices.text: Say only three words

mem.note: said three words at the end

effects.log: You stand at the grave and say: "I was listening." It is enough. The mourners do not understand, and you do not explain.

events.text: You have taken to sitting on the bench by the temple pond in the mornings. So, it turns out, has {npc}. There is only one bench. Neither of you will leave first.

choices.text: Sit at your end and say nothing

effects.log: You sit in silence for an hour. Then two. On the third day {npc} brings a cushion, and does not offer to share it.

choices.text: Bring a chess board

effects.log: You play every morning. You keep a tally scratched into the bench. The monks complain and then join in.

choices.text: Bring a second bench

effects.log: You pay a carpenter 10 taels. {npc} sits on your new bench. You sit on the old one. It is no better.

events.text: The tally scratched into the temple bench is up to four hundred games. The abbot has asked, very politely, whether the two of you would mind not shouting at dawn, because the monks cannot meditate.

choices.text: Play in whispers

effects.log: Whispered chess is somehow more vicious. A young monk learns more about cursing in a week than in a lifetime.

choices.text: Teach the monks to play

effects.log: Within a year, the temple is the strongest chess temple in the province. You and {npc} are its terror.

choices.text: Move the game to {npc}'s house

effects.log: It is not the same. On the third morning you are both back on the bench.

events.text: One morning {npc} is not on the bench. The next morning neither. On the third morning the abbot comes out with a message: {npc} is unwell, and asks if you would bring the board to {his} bed.

choices.text: Bring the board

mem.note: brought the board to my bed

effects.log: You play by the bed. {npc} wins, for the first time in a month, and gets better, out of pure triumph.

choices.text: Bring the bench

effects.log: You and two monks carry the bench across town. {npc} laughs so hard the physician has to sit down.

choices.text: Wait on the bench

effects.log: You wait. A week later {npc} comes back, thin and furious that you kept the game warm without {him}.

events.text: A letter from {npc}, written slowly: "We are old. Every bout these last twenty years has been a game. I would like one more real one, before my hands go. Mount Qing, the morning of the first frost. No physicians. No crowd."

choices.text: Accept

effects.log: You write back one word: "Yes." Then you begin to train, for the first time in years, as if your life depended on it.

choices.text: Accept, and train together beforehand

mem.note: trained with me for our last duel

effects.log: You train side by side for a month, each correcting the other's old faults. It is the strangest preparation for a duel either of you has ever made.

choices.text: Refuse: you will not fight {npc} for real again

effects.log: {npc} does not write again for a year. Then a letter arrives: "Coward. I understand."

events.text: The morning of the first frost on Mount Qing. The sun comes up over the clouds. {npc} is already there, sword drawn, very old, very straight. You bow. {npc} bows.

choices.text: Fight with everything you have

mem.note: fought my last duel with everything

ok.log: You win, on the last exchange, by a hair. {npc} sits down on the frost and laughs until you sit too.

mem.note: fought my last duel with everything

fail.log: {npc} wins, on the last exchange, by a hair. You sit down on the frost and laugh until {npc} sits too.

choices.text: Fight with everything, and stop one move short

effects.log: You both stop one move short, at the same moment. You look at each other's blades. Neither of you will ever know who would have won.

choices.text: Put down your sword and watch the sunrise instead

effects.log: {npc} looks at you, and at the clouds, and puts down a sword for the first time in seventy years.

events.text: {npc} has died, very old, in a house on the slope of Mount Qing. The family has sent you {npc}'s sword, with a note in the old hand: "For the one who knows who won."

choices.text: Take the sword to the peak and leave it there

mem.note: took my sword to the peak

effects.log: You climb slowly, all day. You leave the sword on the rock where you bowed. On the way down the frost begins.

choices.text: Hang it beside your own

effects.log: Two swords on one wall. Visitors ask whose the second is. You tell them: the best fighter you ever met.

choices.text: Give it to a young fighter who reminds you of {npc}

effects.log: The young fighter is insufferable, arrogant and brilliant. Perfect.

events.text: You have bought a burial plot on the sunny side of Cloud Hill, with a view of the river. Within the week, {npc} has bought the plot next to it. The deed says so. {npc} sends you a copy of the deed, with no letter.

choices.text: Buy the plot on the other side too, to be safe

effects.log: You pay 30 taels for the plot on your left. {npc} buys the one on the left of that. Cloud Hill is filling up with your quarrel.

choices.text: Visit {npc} and laugh about it

effects.log: {npc} has already planted a plum tree on the boundary. "So you have something to look at," {npc} says.

choices.text: Sell yours and buy elsewhere

effects.log: You buy on the shady side. {npc} buys on the shady side the following week.

events.text: The stonemason on Cloud Hill has received two orders for tombstones, one from you and one from {npc}, and is in despair: each of you has asked for the taller stone. The stonemason asks you to settle it, please, before the mason dies first.

choices.text: Order two stones exactly the same height

mem.note: made the stones the same height

effects.log: The mason is so relieved that the stones are carved with a little extra, a kite on yours and a carp on {npc}'s.

choices.text: Pay for the taller stone

effects.log: You pay 40 taels. {npc} has the plum tree. The plum tree grows. Within a decade it is taller than any stone.

choices.text: Order one stone for both

mem.note: ordered one stone for us both

effects.log: The mason carves one stone with two names and the words: "Still arguing." {npc} says it is the most sensible thing you have ever done.

events.text: The plum tree between the two plots on Cloud Hill has flowered for the first time. {npc} sends a note: "Come and see it while we can both stand on the right side of the ground."

choices.text: Go and sit under the plum tree

mem.note: sat under the plum tree with me

effects.log: You sit on your own grave and {npc} sits on {his}, and you share a flask of tea and watch the river.

choices.text: Go, and bring a second plum tree

effects.log: Now there are two. Your quarrel has become a little orchard. Children from the village pick the fruit.

choices.text: Write back that you will see it from below one day

effects.log: {npc} writes: "Not before me, you will not." It is the last word of a very long argument. You let {npc} have it.

events.text: Word travels fast in the jianghu: {npc} has gone into closed-door cultivation to break through to the next realm. You are at the same wall, and have been for a year. The teahouses are already asking which of you will come out first.
events.arc: The Same Year, the Same Wall

choices.text: Go into seclusion too, the same week

ok.log: You come out of the cave forty days later, half starved, a little stronger, a few days before {npc}, who hears and goes straight back in.

fail.log: {npc} comes out first, glowing. You come out a week later, smelling of cave.

choices.text: Train in the open, where {npc}'s friends can see you are not worried

effects.log: You train in the town square, in public, very calm. Inside you are not calm at all.

choices.text: Send {npc} a pot of the good tea for the seclusion

effects.log: {npc}'s disciple receives it. {npc} drinks it on the thirtieth day and is so suspicious that it breaks the meditation.

events.text: {npc}'s breakthrough has gone wrong. Qi deviation: {npc} is lying in a dark room, the meridians knotted, and the physicians say only someone of the same school of breathing, someone who knows exactly how {npc} trains, could straighten them. You know exactly how {npc} trains. You have watched for years.
events.arc: The Same Year, the Same Wall

choices.text: Go and guide {npc}'s qi

ok.log: You sit back to back all night, your breath leading {npc}'s round the knot. By dawn it loosens. {npc} sleeps for two days and wakes up angry, which is a good sign.

fail.log: The deviation jumps into you halfway. You both lie in the dark room for a month. You both live.

choices.text: Send the physicians everything you know about {npc}'s training

mem.note: told the physicians how I train

effects.log: You write fourteen pages. The physicians use eleven. {npc} recovers slowly, and reads all fourteen.

choices.text: Stay away: it is too dangerous

effects.log: {npc} recovers slowly, without you, and never asks why.

events.text: Your own breakthrough, years later, is not going well. On the fortieth night of seclusion, a voice at the cave mouth says: "You breathe through the left side too much. You always did. Shall I come in?"
events.arc: The Same Year, the Same Wall

choices.text: Let {npc} in

effects.log: {npc} sits back to back with you, breath leading breath, as you once did. At dawn the wall breaks.

choices.text: Tell {npc} to go away, and do it alone

ok.log: You do it alone, on the forty-fifth night, out of pure spite. {npc} is still at the cave mouth when you come out, asleep.

fail.log: It fails. You come out. {npc} is at the cave mouth, asleep, and wakes, and says nothing, and walks you home.

choices.text: Ask {npc} to stay outside and talk

effects.log: {npc} talks all night through the rock about nothing. Somewhere around the third watch, you stop thinking about the wall.

events.text: A secret realm has opened behind the Nine Dragon Falls for one month only, as it does once a generation. Every young master in the province is going. You arrive at the falls on the first morning. {npc} is already there, soaked to the bone, having been there all night.

choices.text: Go in together, for safety

mem.note: went into the secret realm with me

effects.log: You go in side by side. Inside is a valley of mist and very old trees, and on the far side, a stone pavilion with a single box.

choices.text: Race {npc} through the falls

ok.log: You are through first and see the stone pavilion and the box before anyone.

fail.log: The water knocks you flat. {npc} is through first, and waits for you, which is worse.

choices.text: Wait until the crowd thins

effects.log: You go in on the third day. The valley is quiet. You find {npc} sitting by the pavilion, waiting, the box unopened.

events.text: The box in the stone pavilion behind Nine Dragon Falls holds two things: a pill that glows like a coal and a scroll tied with a black cord. There is room in the realm, the inscription says, for one gift per visitor. {npc} looks at you. You look at {npc}.

choices.text: Take the pill, leave the scroll

effects.log: The pill burns all the way down. {npc} takes the scroll and does not open it until you are both outside.

choices.text: Take the scroll, leave the pill

effects.log: The scroll is a sword method that makes your hands itch. {npc} swallows the pill and glows for a week.

choices.text: Give both to {npc}

mem.note: gave me both gifts of the realm

effects.log: The inscription glows: a gift given in that place counts double. A second pill appears in the box. {npc} stares at it, and at you.

events.text: {npc} has never opened the scroll, or swallowed the pill, or whatever {npc} took from the falls. It has been sitting in a box, and now {npc} has brought it to you. "I never wanted the gift. I wanted to know what you would take."

choices.text: Tell {npc} the truth about why you chose

mem.note: told me why at the falls

effects.log: You tell {npc}. It takes a long time, and involves a kite. {npc} listens to the end and then, finally, opens the box.

choices.text: Take it, and use it

effects.log: It is still good. You are a little stronger. {npc} watches with a strange satisfied face, as though a long game has ended.

choices.text: Throw it into the falls together

mem.note: threw the gift into the falls with me

effects.log: It glows a moment under the water and is gone. You both feel lighter.

events.text: A young fighter turns up at your gate with a challenge and a sharp voice: "My teacher is {npc}. My teacher says you can be beaten. My teacher says it is very important I find out how."

choices.text: Accept the challenge

ok.log: You win in nine moves. The disciple goes home in a fury. {npc} writes: "Nine? You are getting slow."

mem.note: lost to my disciple, and took it well

fail.log: The disciple wins. You are surprised, and proud of {npc}, which surprises you more.

choices.text: Teach the disciple the answer to {npc}'s best move

mem.note: taught my disciple to beat me

effects.log: The disciple goes home and beats {npc} with it. {npc} is incandescent, then fascinated.

choices.text: Send the disciple home with tea and a message

effects.log: Your message to {npc} is: "Come yourself." The disciple delivers it with great relish.

events.text: {npc}'s disciple is back, older, quieter, with a real problem: {npc} has been challenged to a death duel by a man from a rival school and has accepted. The disciple cannot stop it. "You are the only one my teacher has ever listened to, even when not listening."

choices.text: Go and stop the duel

ok.log: You find {npc} at the duelling ground and talk until the other side withdraws, laughing at the two of you. {npc} is furious with you and alive.

fail.log: You fail. You stand as {npc}'s second instead. {npc} wins, barely.

choices.text: Fight the challenger yourself first

roll.foeName: the challenger from the rival school

ok.log: You meet the challenger at dawn and put an end to it. {npc} arrives at noon to find nothing to fight. The disciple is delighted.

fail.log: You lose, badly, and live. The challenger's honour is satisfied. {npc} sits by your bed every day for a month.

choices.text: Tell the disciple it is {npc}'s choice

effects.log: {npc} wins the duel, alone. The disciple stops writing to you.

events.text: {npc}'s disciple has become a master with disciples of their own, and sends you a note: "My teacher is old now, and stubborn, and will not tell me what you two were like when young. Please come and tell my students. My teacher will be in the back, pretending not to listen."

choices.text: Go and tell the students everything

mem.note: told my disciple's students about us

effects.log: You tell them about the kites and the duels and the cave. {npc} interrupts from the back eleven times. The students learn more from the interruptions.

choices.text: Go, and tell only the flattering parts

effects.log: You tell the students what a great fighter {npc} was. From the back, {npc} coughs, and leaves, and is seen wiping an eye.

choices.text: Send a letter for the students instead

effects.log: The letter is read aloud. {npc} snatches it and reads the last page alone.

events.text: At a summit of the righteous sects, the head of the Iron Palm School collapses after a cup of tea, poisoned. Two people were seen near the teapot: you and {npc}. The hall turns to look at you both.

choices.text: Defend {npc} as well as yourself

effects.log: You stand side by side and swear before the hall. The Iron Palm elders are not satisfied, but they hesitate.

choices.text: Point out that {npc} poured the tea

effects.log: {npc} did pour the tea. {npc} did not poison it. The look {npc} gives you is not one you will forget.

choices.text: Demand the cup be tested

ok.log: You test the dregs. The poison is a slow one: it was given hours before, at breakfast. Neither of you was at breakfast.

fail.log: You cannot tell what it is. The hall argues all night.

events.text: The Iron Palm head is alive, barely, and the summit has given you and {npc} ten days to find the poisoner before both of you are named. {npc} comes to your room at midnight: "I have a name. I need a witness nobody will doubt is my enemy."

choices.text: Go with {npc}

mem.note: caught the summit poisoner with me

ok.log: The poisoner is an Iron Palm elder who wanted the head's seat. You catch the elder burning letters. The summit is saved and stunned.

mem.note: caught the summit poisoner with me

fail.log: The elder's guards fight hard. You drag the elder before the summit in the morning, bloodied, with half the letters.

choices.text: Go to the summit leaders instead

mem.note: went to the leaders behind my back

effects.log: The leaders arrest the elder on {npc}'s evidence. {npc} gets the credit and is annoyed you did not trust {him}.

choices.text: Refuse: it could be a trap

effects.log: It is not a trap. {npc} catches the poisoner alone. The summit thanks {npc}. You are thanked as an afterthought.

events.text: The Iron Palm School, grateful, has opened its library to the two who caught the poisoner at the summit, for one day each year, on the same day. The librarian asks only that you do not fight in the stacks.

choices.text: Read side by side, in silence

mem.note: read in the Iron Palm library with me

effects.log: Every year on that day, the library has two old readers in it. They fight only about who gets the window.

choices.text: Race to read the best manual first

mem.note: got to the best manual first

ok.log: You get it. {npc} gets the second best and reads it twice as hard.

fail.log: {npc} gets it. You find, in the corner, a forgotten book that is better.

choices.text: Give your day to a young student

effects.log: The student is overwhelmed. {npc} gives a day to a student too, and the two students become rivals at once.

events.text: The old village teacher who taught you both to read and both to fight, badly, has died. You arrive at the grave at the same moment as {npc}, each with a bundle of incense. The teacher's house is to be sold to pay for the funeral.

choices.text: Pay for the funeral together

mem.note: paid for the teacher's funeral with me

effects.log: You pay 40 taels each. The teacher is buried well, and the house is kept for whoever comes next.

choices.text: Pay for it all, before {npc} can

mem.note: paid for the teacher's funeral before me

effects.log: You pay 80 taels. {npc} buys the house the next day, out of spite, and opens it as a school.

choices.text: Offer to sort through the teacher's papers

effects.log: In the papers is a sheet from forty years ago: two children's handwriting exercises, side by side, both marked "Better."

events.text: The old teacher's house has become a village school, run by whichever of you is in the village at the time. The children complain that the two teachers teach the same lesson in opposite ways.

choices.text: Teach a lesson together, side by side

effects.log: You argue in front of the children for an hour. The children have never learned so much about how to argue.

choices.text: Write the lessons down so they match

effects.log: The lessons match. They are worse. The children prefer the arguments.

choices.text: Leave the school to {npc}

effects.log: {npc} runs it well. On the wall is the old sheet: "Better. Better."

events.text: Two children from the village school have been accepted into a great sect, the first ever from the village. Their parents have asked "both teachers" to see them off at the crossroads.

choices.text: See them off with {npc}

mem.note: saw the children off with me

effects.log: The children bow to you both. As they go, one of them shouts back: "We are rivals now, like you!" {npc} looks at you, horrified, and then laughs.

choices.text: Give each child a gift

effects.log: You give each a good brush, 20 taels in all. {npc} gives each a good sword. You argue about which was the wiser gift all the way home.

choices.text: Tell the children something true

effects.log: You tell them: "Find someone who is always just a little better. Then never thank them." {npc} snorts.

events.text: You have outlived everyone who knew why you and {npc} were rivals. The teahouses of a new century tell a story about two masters who have hated each other for a hundred years, and none of the details are right. {npc} has sent you the latest version, annotated.

choices.text: Annotate it back

mem.note: annotated the century story with me

effects.log: Your notes are longer than the story. {npc}'s notes on your notes are longer still. The teahouse buys them both.

choices.text: Go to the teahouse and tell the real story

effects.log: Nobody believes a word. The real story is too strange: kites and frogs and a bridge. They prefer the hatred.

choices.text: Ask {npc} what the rivalry was about, really

effects.log: {npc} thinks for a long time. "I think," {npc} writes, "we were afraid there was no one else who would keep up."

events.text: A hundred and some years of rivalry. A young cultivator, curious, has come to you with a question that has become a scholarly dispute: who is ahead? Who has won more? The young one has a ledger of every recorded bout, and the count is exactly even.

choices.text: Ask the young one to burn the ledger

effects.log: The ledger burns. {npc}, when told, is outraged: "I wanted to know too!"

choices.text: Arrange one more bout to break the tie

ok.log: You win. The ledger is uneven by one. {npc} is already planning the next bout.

fail.log: {npc} wins. The ledger is uneven by one. You are already planning the next bout.

choices.text: Add a line at the bottom: "Draw. Forever."

effects.log: {npc} writes underneath, in a hand a century old: "Agreed. Except the kite."

events.text: Somewhere along the centuries, without either of you saying it, the rivalry became the oldest friendship in the jianghu. {npc} has proposed a contest to mark the date: who can remember more about the other, in a hundred questions.

choices.text: Accept the contest

ok.log: You win by three questions. {npc} disputes two of them. You let {npc} have one.

fail.log: {npc} wins by three. You dispute two of them. {npc} lets you have one.

choices.text: Answer every question with "the kite"

effects.log: It is correct more often than you would think.

choices.text: Refuse: some things you would rather keep

effects.log: {npc} understands. Some things are not for contests.

events.text: A fever has closed the village of Stone Mill. The county has roped it off, and nobody goes in. You hear that {npc} went in three days ago with a pack of medicine and has not come out.

choices.text: Go in after {npc}

ok.log: You find {npc} boiling herbs in the temple, grey with exhaustion. Together you hold the fever back for a month. Stone Mill lives.

fail.log: You catch the fever on the second day. {npc} nurses you and the village both. You all live, barely.

choices.text: Send in supplies over the ropes

effects.log: You pay 50 taels for rice and herbs and throw them over the ropes every morning. {npc} catches them and waves.

choices.text: Stay out: it is madness

effects.log: {npc} comes out after a month, thin and alive, and walks past you without stopping.

events.text: Stone Mill has recovered from the fever. Its people have carved a stone at the village gate with one name: {npc}'s. Under it, smaller, a carver has added "and another", because nobody can remember the second name.

choices.text: Laugh, and leave it

mem.note: left the stone as it was

effects.log: "And another" becomes your name in Stone Mill. Children call it to you in the street.

choices.text: Ask for your name to be added

mem.note: wanted a name on the stone

effects.log: The carver adds it, very small. {npc} visits and says it is too big.

choices.text: Ask that {npc}'s name be taken off too, for the dead

mem.note: gave the stone to the dead

effects.log: The stone is recarved with the names of those who died. {npc} stands beside you and reads every one.

events.text: The fever has come back, to a different village, and the county has sent for "the two who saved Stone Mill." {npc} is already on the road, and has left a message at your gate: "Bring the big kettle."

choices.text: Go, with the big kettle

ok.log: You know what to do now, both of you. The fever does not get a foothold.

fail.log: It is harder this time. You are older. You still win.

choices.text: Send your best student with the kettle

effects.log: Your student arrives with {npc}'s student. The two students do very well, and are rivals within the week.

choices.text: Send silver for physicians

effects.log: You pay 50 taels. {npc} writes afterwards: "The kettle was missed."

events.text: The court painter is painting The Hundred Heroes of the Age for the emperor. You and {npc} have both been chosen, and must sit for the painter on the same day in the same hall, because the painter is in a hurry and short of chairs.
events.arc: The Painting of the Hundred Heroes

choices.text: Sit politely

effects.log: You both sit perfectly still for six hours, glaring. The painter is delighted: it is the most intense pair in the whole painting.

choices.text: Make {npc} laugh during the sitting

mem.note: made me laugh at the sitting

effects.log: {npc} cracks on the fourth hour. In the finished painting, one of the hundred heroes is laughing. It is the only one people remember.

choices.text: Bribe the painter to make you taller

effects.log: You pay 20 taels. {npc} paid 30. You are both very tall. The emperor asks if the painter has been drinking.

events.text: The Hundred Heroes has been hung in the palace, and you have both been summoned to see it. The emperor, standing in front of you and {npc}, asks which of you is the greater.
events.arc: The Painting of the Hundred Heroes

choices.text: Answer: {npc}

mem.note: named me the greater before the emperor

effects.log: The emperor raises an eyebrow and asks {npc} the same question. {npc} names you. The emperor laughs and gives you both a jade token.

choices.text: Answer: yourself

mem.note: named yourself greater before the emperor

effects.log: The emperor looks at {npc}, who names {him}self too. The emperor laughs and gives you each half a jade token.

choices.text: Answer: neither, alone

effects.log: The emperor, pleased with the answer, has the two of you moved closer together in the painting.

events.text: The Hundred Heroes is cracking with age. The court is copying it. The copyist, it turns out, is the great-grandchild of the original painter, and sends you a letter: "Of the hundred, only the two of you are still alive. Would you sit again, so that the copy is true?"
events.arc: The Painting of the Hundred Heroes

choices.text: Sit again, beside {npc}

mem.note: sat for the copy with me

effects.log: Two old heroes in a hall full of the dead, glaring for six hours. The copyist paints exactly what is there.

choices.text: Ask to be painted laughing this time

effects.log: You both laugh. The copy has two laughing heroes. The court is scandalised. The copy is adored.

choices.text: Decline: let the old faces stand

effects.log: The copy keeps your young faces. {npc} sits alone, and asks the copyist to paint an empty chair beside.
